title: much / many · a little / a few

units.title: much / many
units.rule: *many* — "koʻp": sanaladigan koʻplikdagi otlar bilan (*many apples, many books*). *much* — "koʻp": sanalmaydigan otlar bilan (*much water, much money*). Ularni asosan soʻroq va inkor gaplarda ishlatamiz: *How many apples are there? There isn't much milk.* Darak gapda *a lot of* ishlatamiz: *I have got a lot of books.* *How many…?* — "nechta?", *How much…?* — "qancha?"
examples: How many books have you got?
I have got a lot of friends.

text.title: At the market
text.en:
Malika: Aziz, how many apples do you want?
Aziz: I want five apples. How much are they?
Malika: They are not expensive. Have we got much money?
Aziz: No, we haven't got much money. But we have got a lot of bread at home.
Malika: There are many people at the market today.
Aziz: Yes, there are a lot of people. Look, there isn't much water in the bottle.

units.title: a little / a few
units.rule: *a few* — "bir nechta, ozgina": sanaladigan koʻplikdagi otlar bilan (*a few apples, a few friends*). *a little* — "bir oz, ozgina": sanalmaydigan otlar bilan (*a little water, a little time*). Ikkalasi ham darak gapda ishlatiladi va "oz, lekin yetarli" maʼnosini beradi: *I have got a few friends in Tashkent. There is a little milk in the fridge.*
examples: I have got a few friends in Tashkent.
There are a few apples on the table.
There is a little milk in the fridge.
Bekzod has got a few books.
We have got a little time.

text.title: Dinner at home
text.en: Nodira cooks dinner. She has got a little rice and a few potatoes. There is a little meat in the fridge. She puts a little salt in the food. Karim comes home. He is tired. He drinks a few cups of tea. Hamida eats a little bread. Bekzod has got a few friends at home. They eat dinner together.
